restrictions: SCOPE: NOT A NATIVE 32-BIT SYSTEM. The 32-bit (i686, gcc -m32) executable was built and run only inside the Ubuntu 24.04.5 WSL2 distribution with WSLg on a Windows 11 laptop (validation/platforms/linux-i686.json): a 64-bit (x86_64) kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 runs it in compatibility mode on an x86_64 CPU (Intel Core i5-8300H) through the i386 multiarch libraries (libc6:i386 2.39, libx11-6:i386, libxft2:i386, libfontconfig1:i386; dpkg --print-foreign-architectures prints i386). Not tested: a 32-bit kernel, a 32-bit-only distribution, a CPU without x86_64, a real or old machine, any other X server (Xorg, a native Wayland session), any window manager decoration, any system older than Ubuntu 24.04. Per ADR 0007 the executable is built on the machine that runs it, so no glibc or libstdc++ ceiling is checked. This verdict says that the 32-bit build of the UI links and runs here; it does not determine the Linux floor and says nothing about T092 beyond this platform.

SAME SOURCE, SAME LIMITS AS THE x86_64 BUILD: the UI sources are those of validation/verdicts/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64-legacy.json, built with -m32. By decision (accepted by the owner) there is no text shaping and no bidirectional layout (logical order, left to right); the stored screenshot of that verdict shows it for the x86_64 build, and no new picture of the i686 build was stored, so the i686 drawing of Hebrew, Arabic and ZWJ sequences is not backed by an i686 screenshot. A code point that no installed font has (U+0378 in the mixed string) is an empty box and the probe line carries 'missing-glyph': measured on this build (run log). Which glyphs exist depends on the fonts of this machine.

CORE-FONT PATH ONLY WITHOUT XFT: the executable of this verdict was built with libxft-dev:i386 and libfontconfig-dev:i386 present, so it draws through Xft. Before those packages were installed the i686 build took the core X11 font path (fallback xlib-core-font-glyphs, probe line with 'glyph-substitution', stored in xlib-core-font-fallback-i686-probe-mixed.txt). In this session that path was exercised for the vectors only (LOOMORA_XLIB_NO_XFT=1, 15 of 15), not for the mixed string.

INPUT WAS SYNTHETIC: the window run typed 'Marie' with XSendEvent key events from xlib-driver.c on the WSLg X server, never a physical keyboard or a real layout; no input-method server, dead key, compose sequence or IME was tried. The 1,000-character limit was checked through the vectors only (2 truncated vectors passed), not by typing in the window.

ONE VECTOR RUN FAILED ON AN X SERVER ERROR: in the stored run of tools/run_vectors.py, 4 of the 15 vectors (empty, ascii, ascii_punctuation, accented, the first four launched in parallel) failed with 'XIO: fatal IO error 2 on X server ":0"' at 0.0 s; 5 repeated runs of the same executable and 3 runs of the x86_64 build then passed 15 of 15. The cause was not investigated (a WSLg display connection problem is likely, not proven); it was not seen on the x86_64 build, which was only run 3 times, so a difference between the two builds is not excluded.

ONE RUN, ONE DAY: the numbers are one run on 2026-11-14 (two probe lines stored); no series was made, display_ms and peak_rss_kb are indicative only. The display was WSLg :0; no private Xvfb display was used.
disabled_features: missing-glyph (Xft path, the normal path of this build: only a code point that no installed font has, such as U+0378, is drawn as an empty box; the greeting and the probe record are unchanged. Measured in run-log.txt)

glyph-substitution (core-font path, NOT taken by the build of this verdict: only when CMake finds no 32-bit libXft and fontconfig development files, LOOMORA_XLIB_XFT=OFF or the run-time switch LOOMORA_XLIB_NO_XFT; fallback xlib-core-font-glyphs, platform_ids empty on purpose. Measured on the earlier i686 build in xlib-core-font-fallback-i686-probe-mixed.txt)
text-shaping-and-bidi (not implemented, by decision: logical order, left to right, isolated Arabic forms, ZWJ sequences drawn as components; no probe marker exists for it)

notes: Verdict of the 32-bit (i686) Linux Legacy UI (Xlib, C++11, CMake, text drawn with Xft and fontconfig) on linux-i686, written 2026-11-14 after a real run of the rebuilt executable in WSL (run-log.txt), modelled on validation/verdicts/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64-legacy.json. STATUS ok_restricted because the greeting 'Bonjour Coucou' / 'Bonjour Marie' and the mixed Unicode input are computed and displayed by the 32-bit build (greeting_matches true, displayed true in both probe lines; 15 of 15 vectors in every run made except the first stored one, which had 4 failures on an X server connection error), but the restrictions are real: not a native 32-bit system, no shaping or bidi, an empty box for a glyph no font has, the core-font path only without 32-bit Xft at build time, one machine under WSLg, synthetic key events, one run. DECISION keep: nothing found makes the UI unusable on this platform. FALLBACKS (validation/fallbacks.json): cxx17-nodiscard is taken (deliverable record); xlib-core-font-glyphs is NOT taken by this build. BUILD AND CHECK COMMANDS (inside WSL, Ubuntu 24.04, build directory under $HOME/loomora-build): 'python3 tools/build.py linux legacy --arch i686' (needs gcc-multilib, g++-multilib, libx11-dev:i386, libxft-dev:i386, libfontconfig-dev:i386), then the probe, 'python3 tools/run_vectors.py linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64 legacy --exe <executable>' and the window driver; the probe line carries the platform_id of the host (linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64), not linux-i686, because the application derives it from /etc/os-release and uname. build.py rewrites the deliverable record without its measured fields and its VERIFIED text: that rewrite was discarded, the stored record is unchanged. The replayable procedure is validation/procedures/linux.md (field 'reproduction'). The text of the run log keeps its LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes) because this verdict holds its sha256. NOT DONE and not claimed: a native 32-bit kernel or distribution, an i686-only CPU, any other system, X server or font set, a physical keyboard or an input-method server, shaping or bidirectional text (none by decision), a series of runs, a screenshot stored for i686, and the end-of-life banner on an end-of-life system. SPEC 002, THE .loomora PROJECT FILE (2026-11-17). HOST NOTE: the spec 002 runs were made on a host with an Intel Core i7-11800H (16 logical CPUs), not on the MSI GL63 8RD of validation/platforms/windows-11-x64.json (the Windows build, 26300.9974, is the same). BUILD AND RUN NOTE: the i686 build (cmake/toolchains/linux-gcc-i686.cmake, g++ 15.2.0 -m32) was run as a 32-bit process on the 64-bit kernel of the WSL2 distribution Ubuntu-26.04, NOT in the Ubuntu 24.04 distribution that this record describes, and not on a native 32-bit system. FORMAT RESULT: loomora_format_selftest passes, ctest 3 of 3 (selftest, format_selftest and the Catch2 loomora_tests built and passed for i686). A FIRST RUN WITHOUT THE SSE2 SWITCH FAILED: 32-bit GCC computes doubles on the x87 unit with 80-bit intermediates, so the fixtures (cos, sin, round3, 0.1 + 0.2) gave other values: loomora_format_selftest reported multi and multi-light different (multi sha256 b1f56507a80d99fef862f0f889b253881ffd69079b3f87977b45ff8913a86333, multi-light 10f8dfc2fc23f0105f91dc365862e3642e0e5907666891e36071e5b6bf8808dd; basic, empty, escape40 and one identical) and loomora_tests had two failures (write_double(0.1 + 0.2) gave 0.3; the nails of layout 2). -ffloat-store alone was not enough. With LOOMORA_TEST_FP_FLAGS = -msse2 -mfpmath=sse on the TEST programs only (fallback x87-double-fixtures) all six reference files are byte-identical to Linux x86_64, with libloomora itself still compiled for x87, so the product code needs no switch (spike S-F2; hashes and the two x87 files in validation/evidence/adr-0021/linux-i686/). file_posix.cpp also compiles with LOOMORA_FMT_LSEEK64=1 and LOOMORA_FMT_NO_LARGE_FILES=1 under -m32 (compile only). SC-010: the project modes of the Legacy UI were NOT run on the i686 build (the project-mode run covered the UIs of the default x86-64 build only: see the x86_64 verdict). NOT DONE and not claimed: a native 32-bit kernel or CPU without SSE2, the UI project modes, a fuzz run.
